The graph consists of three parts: the line segment for $x\in [-2,-1],$ the line segment for $x\in (-1,1),$ and the line segment for $x\in (1,3].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={{{\int }_{-2}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-2,-1].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle. Therefore, we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1\cdot 3) \\  & =1.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{1}=-1.5.
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (-1,1).$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2+3)(2) \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (1,3].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1+2)(2) \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-{A}_{1}+{A}_{2}+{A}_{3} \\  & =-1.5+5+3 \\  & =6.5.\end{aligned}
$$
